findings.title: Reject conflicting highest-priority crypto providers
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200. Removing the multiple-provider error therefore allows conflicting full providers and selects whichever ServiceLoader enumerates first. For example, when both default and FIPS providers are visible, the non-FIPS provider can win and FIPS is merely logged as ignored; this configuration previously failed initialization. Retain conflict detection for multiple highest-priority providers, while allowing the lower-priority authz fallback, so classpath ordering cannot silently determine FIPS behavior.

findings.title: Validate the concatenated ECDSA signature length
findings.body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER copies exactly signLength bytes without checking signature.length. Consequently, a valid ES256 signature with arbitrary bytes appended converts to exactly the same valid DER signature rather than being rejected. JOSE requires an exact signature length of 64, 96, or 132 bytes, depending on the algorithm. Reject mismatched lengths with IOException before copying; otherwise callers relying on this converter accept malformed, overlong signatures.

findings.title: Provide a backward-compatible default for order()
findings.body: Adding order() as an abstract method breaks existing ServiceLoader CryptoProvider implementations compiled against the previous interface. Such a provider can still be instantiated, but loading it alongside the newly registered authz provider makes the sorting comparator invoke the missing method and throw AbstractMethodError, preventing AuthzClient creation. A default implementation with an appropriate baseline priority would preserve existing providers while allowing implementations to override their ordering.

findings.title: Exercise the actual curves required by each ECDSA algorithm
findings.body: The tests generate an uninitialized EC key pair, which on the normal JDK defaults to P-256, and reuse that curve for ES384 and ES512. Those tests therefore only pad P-256 signature values into larger buffers; they never exercise full-width P-384/P-521 values or the long-form DER sequence length required by P-521 signatures. Initialize the key generator with the algorithm-specific curve and verify the reconstructed DER signature against the original data, rather than only comparing values after the first conversion.
